newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police release 11 suspected Islamists.
newsitem.headline: French police release 11 suspected Islamists.

text.p: French authorities on Friday released without charge 11 people detained earlier this week in a round-up initially trumpeted by police as a crackdown against Islamic militant groups.
Sources close to the investigation told reporters that searches at the homes of the suspects failed to uncover incriminating evidence, though one shotgun was seized.

The 11 were detained on Wednesday in Paris suburbs with large North African Arab immigrant populations. Police said then that the swoops were aimed at rooting out an Islamist network which allegedly helped Lionel Dumont, a gangster with fundamentalist extremist ties, flee France for Bosnia after evading a police shootout in the northern city of Roubaix in March 1996.

Four other people, suspected of being part of a gang of guerrillas who organised robberies to finance fundamentalist activities, died in the Roubaix shootout when the house in which they were hiding caught fire and burned to the ground.
After evading police for a year, Dumont was detained in Bosnia in March after allegedly trying to hold up a petrol station and carrying out unspecified "terrorist" acts.

France has been the target of a string of bombings claimed by Algerian extremists. The most recent was last December, when a bomb at the Port Royal underground station in Paris killed four people and injured dozens.
